environment.description: Same Spring Boot application on EC2 behind ALB, but the ALB security group ingress on port 443 is restricted to the CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). A CloudFront distribution is configured with a custom origin pointing to the ALB, with Origin Access Control (OAC) disabled but a CloudFront KeyGroup attached to a cache behavior requiring signed URLs (Trusted Key Groups policy). The CloudFront distribution's cache behavior for /api/* has Viewer Protocol Policy: HTTPS Only, and the Trusted Key Groups setting mandates that every request to /api/* must carry a valid CloudFront signed URL (Policy, Signature, Key-Pair-Id query parameters or equivalent cookies). Requests without a valid signature receive a 403 from CloudFront edge. The signing key pair is a 2048-bit RSA key managed in AWS Secrets Manager, rotated every 90 days, accessible only to the internal API gateway service via IAM role with condition key aws:SourceVpc. Additionally, the ALB has a custom header validation rule: CloudFront adds a header X-Origin-Verify with a secret token (stored in Secrets Manager, rotated monthly), and the ALB listener rule only forwards requests where this header matches the expected value — all other requests get a fixed 403 response.

config.cloudfront_distribution: E2XYZABC123DEF with cache behavior /api/* requiring Trusted Key Groups
config.key_group: kg-9f8e7d6c with RSA-2048 public key, private key in Secrets Manager
config.signing_requirement: all /api/* requests must have valid Policy+Signature+Key-Pair-Id params
config.alb_security_group: sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f, ingress only from com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
config.alb_custom_header_rule: X-Origin-Verify header must match rotating secret, else 403
config.direct_alb_access: blocked by security group prefix list restriction
